maria: Hey team — customer reported they can no longer open the project console (gets 403). Problem started right after our IdP SCIM job ran this morning. Can we triage?

alice: Can you share the exact error they see and steps to repro? Also need project id + affected user email.

maria: Repro steps: 1) log into console via SSO 2) switch to org X -> open project UI -> 403. Error from API: `{ "error": "forbidden", "message": "user lacks project:view" }`
Curl we ran:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <session>" https://console.redwood.ai/api/projects/px-0a1b2c3d --fail -i```
Project id: px-0a1b2c3d, affected user: jane.doe@example.com

ben: Thanks. Any recent SCIM/group mapping changes? I see a SCIM sync at 07:03 that renamed group `eng-team-x` -> `eng-team-x-prod` per IdP. That can break role inheritance if our group->role mapping was keyed to the old name.

kevin: Also check role-propagation queue. Sometimes the background worker that applies SCIM deltas fails midway and leaves members orphaned for a bit. Can you paste `GET /internal/authz/membership?project=px-0a1b2c3d&user=jane.doe@example.com` response (can redact tokens)?

maria: Pasted output (redacted): ```{ "project": "px-0a1b2c3d", "user": "jane.doe@example.com", "roles": [] }```

alice: That confirms the user lost membership. Likely two factors: 1) SCIM renamed the group so mapping no longer matched, 2) propagation worker didn't rebuild the project role index. Quick workaround: add the user directly to project with `project:viewer` to restore access. Longer fix: re-run role-propagation for the project.

ben: I will request a manual SCIM resync + mapping reconciliation. For the longer fix, run the rebuild job: `./bin/authz_rebuild --project px-0a1b2c3d --force` on auth-master. This will re-evaluate group claims and reapply inherited roles.

kevin: I can run that now. Will schedule a short window — should be fast but may bump caches. Confirm: do we have approval to touch prod auth index?

maria: Customer is OK with a short maintenance window. Please proceed, Kevin.

kevin: Running: `./bin/authz_rebuild --project px-0a1b2c3d --force` ...
deploy-bot: authz_rebuild job started by kevin at 2026-03-17T14:12:30Z, job id: jb-984311
kevin: Job logs: 
- fetched SCIM delta: group rename `eng-team-x` -> `eng-team-x-prod`
- reconciled mapping: applied mapping alias for `eng-team-x-prod` -> role `project:viewer`
- re-applied inherited roles to members (n=48)
- finished in 12.3s

deploy-bot: authz_rebuild job jb-984311 completed successfully (exit 0)

maria: Re-tested with the user — jane.doe@example.com can now open the project console. No 403. :white_check_mark:

alice: I'll follow up to add a defensive alias rule in SCIM mapping logic so future renames don't orphan mappings (rule: map by group id if present, fallback to name, and keep a group-alias table). Filed ticket RDW-1589.

ben: Will also add monitoring alert for `role-propagation` failures — currently we only alert on queue backlog, not partial failures.

kevin: Note for runbook: if customer-facing issue, prefer manual `authz_rebuild` over ad-hoc direct grants, then revert any temporary direct grants.

maria: Marking this resolved from support side. Closing thread.
